key_insight: In a large health check-up cohort, chest X-ray AI generally matched routine radiologist reads and was especially sensitive for nodules/masses, with exploratory signs of earlier lung cancer flagging in some confirmed cases.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI could help triage or support chest radiograph review in screening workflows, but prospective benefit and downstream impact still need confirmation.
method: Retrospective single-centre study of 298,991 chest radiographs from 114,866 people (2019–2023).
Compared a commercial chest radiography AI against routine double-reading by board-certified radiologists.
Ran two prespecified analyses: any-finding positivity and nodule/mass-focused positivity at manufacturer threshold 15.
evidence_signal: Against routine radiologist interpretation, AI sensitivity/specificity were 72.0%/79.6% for the all-score analysis and 87.1%/91.8% for the nodule-focused analysis, with very high NPV.
watch_item: Because the reference standard was routine radiologist judgment rather than universal CT or pathology, these results reflect operational concordance and retrospective signals rather than proven clinical benefit.
paper_title: Chest Radiography AI Concordance and Lung Cancer Linkage in a Large Health Check-up Cohort
